jurisdiction.text: Australian policy jurisdiction (ISO 3166 AU), not the booking jurisdiction.

screening_threshold.text: Owner input D01 (possible-match score) as used by the KYC reference policy.

ownership_threshold.text: AML/CTF Rules: a beneficial owner is an individual who ultimately owns, directly or indirectly, 25 percent or more of the customer, or controls it.

sanctions_ownership.text: Australian sanctions laws prohibit dealing with assets owned or controlled by a designated person or entity; DFAT guidance treats ownership and control case by case.

control_bases.text: AML/CTF Rules: control includes control through trusts, agreements, arrangements, understandings and practices, whether or not having legal or equitable force, and through the capacity to determine decisions about financial and operating policies.

sanctions_control_bases.text: Majority voting control by a designated person always counts as sanctions control.

verification_methods.text: Institution appetite: a government identity document for individuals and a registry extract for legal entities.

active_registry_statuses.text: Only an active registration verifies legal existence (canonical status vocabulary, upper case).

freshness_seconds.text: Credit decisions rely on identity verification no older than 60 days.

required_screening_types.text: Merchant risk includes reputational and fraud exposure, so adverse media is screened.

required_screening_lists.text: The DFAT Consolidated List of persons and entities subject to Australian sanctions.

screening_roles.text: A guarantor stands behind the credit and is screened. Anyone holding a power of attorney over a payment account or card can move funds and is screened.

pep_scope.text: The AML/CTF Rules cover domestic, foreign and international organisation politically exposed persons.

required_party_roles.text: Every jurisdiction's parties, and, as institution appetite, a trust is onboarded only with at least one named trustee, who holds its legal title and acts for it.

dual_control_required.text: Institution appetite: two independent people approve every onboarding decision a person makes; only the low-risk carve-out (automatic_approval_low_risk) decides without one.

automatic_approval_enabled.text: No pack approves a customer without a person.

automatic_approval_low_risk.text: SYNTHETIC placeholder, not a real institution's appetite: the disposition checkpoint may approve a low-risk case without a person. Every other decision needs dual control.

low_risk_max_factor_score.text: SYNTHETIC placeholder: a case is low risk only when every risk factor scores at or below 0.20 (the corpus's clean individual, H01, scores at most 0.05).

automatic_decline_enabled.text: No pack declines a customer without a person.

diligence_floors.text: No floor: a cell's level comes from the institution's diligence matrix. Layers may only raise floors (keys are customer type or *, then product or *).

mandatory_overlays.text: No overlay is mandatory everywhere; layers add the escalations their regulator requires.

simplified_due_diligence_permitted.text: Institution decision pending: simplified due diligence is not adopted until the policy owner approves where it applies, so an SDD cell is applied as CDD.

knownDifferences.text: Australian law has no fixed percentage test: assets owned or controlled by a designated person are affected, assessed case by case. The library's ofac_50_percent rule flags aggregated majority ownership only; control without majority ownership must reach review through screening.sanctions.control.evaluate. The owner must confirm this mapping.
The 2024 amendments to the AML/CTF Act and the new AML/CTF Rules restate beneficial ownership; this layer follows the pre-reform 25 percent definition until the owner confirms the current text.
